summary: Wooden tower of 1911 replaced by a 1917 Aermotor steel tower on Blue Mountain at Indian Lake; closed 1990, volunteer-restored, NRHP-listed 2001, open with summer stewards.

facts.design: 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with a 7 x 7 ft steel cab, built 1917 to replace a 1911 wooden tower

access.note: Open to the public after restoration; a summit steward is hired each summer under a town and state agreement, per the 2018 NHLR visit report.

visit.trail_note: Marked hiking trail with a large parking area at the trailhead; the Adirondack region listing gives 4 miles round trip and about 1,560 feet of climbing.

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: Site used as a station in the land survey of 1870.
Wooden tower built on the site.
Present 35-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower with 7 x 7 ft steel cab built by the state.
Tower remained active until 1990, when the state closed it; one of the last operating fire towers in New York at that point.
Tower rehabilitated; staffed by volunteers of the Blue Mountain Fire Tower Committee afterwards.
Date registered July 6, 1995 per the NHLR detail page.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places on September 23, 2001, as Blue Mountain Fire Observation Station (NRHP 01001035).
Communications equipment and the building beneath the tower removed in fall 2017.
Tower returned to its historical appearance by the NYSDEC.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the brochure give a wooden tower in 1911, replaced by the current steel tower in 1917. Wikipedia and the NRHP record give 1917 for the steel tower, which matches. The story uses both dates.
NHLR and Wikipedia both describe a 35-foot tower (about 10.7 m). A brochure table gives a 60-foot Aermotor, but its layout is too mixed to tie that figure to this tower, so it is not used.
NHLR and the brochure name NYSDEC or NYS DEC as the builder in 1917. The story says 'the state' rather than naming an agency for that year.

notes_for_editor: Dates are solid: the 1911 wooden tower and 1917 steel tower (NHLR, brochure, Wikipedia), 1990 closure, 1994 rehabilitation, 1995 NHLR registration, and 2001 NRHP listing. Current status rests on an undated Fire Tower Challenge brochure and a commercial listing, so re-check opening status and the summer steward programme before relying on it. The brochure layout mixes several towers, so only its single-line statements are quoted. The NHLR 2018 visit report notes plans to repaint and redeck in 2018; the outcome was not found. The NRHP nomination PDF is not digitized (NPGallery says so), so no nomination text was used. The Blue Mountain Fire Observation Station Wikipedia entry gives a 1975 observer cabin and 1960s radar remains; not used. No photos were added.
